paragraphs: Rav Chama bar Adda, the messenger of Zion, chapter Ein Tzadin: “whoever did not go up to Jerusalem in R. Yochanan's days” [the source's difficult opening]. Yuchasin has a scribal error, for Ein Tzadin, Beitzah 25b, reads: Rav Nachman said to Chama bar Adda, messenger of Zion—Rashi explains that he regularly went up to Jerusalem—“When you go up there, go around by the Ladder of Tyre and go to R. Yaakov bar Idi, and ask him, etc.” Before he arrived, R. Yaakov bar Idi died; he found R. Zerika. As for Rashi's explanation “Lechama bar Adda—this was his name”: if he means that Chama was his name, many are named Chama. If he means Lechama was his name, it requires investigation, since the lamed is a prefixed preposition. Arukh reads shelatziyon, explaining it as “messenger of Zion,” who regularly went to the Land of Israel. End of quotation.
